content.title: About
content.content: A turnover (also called a hot pocket) with ham is a ready‑to‑heat baked snack made of flaky pastry filled with diced cooked ham, sometimes combined with cheese and spices. It can be stored in the fridge or freezer and cooked in a microwave or oven in just a few minutes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turnovers originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a quick snack for factory workers.
In Russia similar items are often called “pocket pies” and are sold in chain supermarkets.
The pastry is usually laminated, giving the product a crisp texture after heating.
The ham filling can be smoked or simply boiled, depending on the brand.
The product is frequently included in “quick‑meal” packs for students and office workers.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Ham provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat products like ham are good sources of heme iron, supporting normal blood formation.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the pastry and protein from the ham rapidly replenishes energy stores.

items.title: Convenient and portable
items.content: A turnover is easy to carry and does not require additional utensils to eat.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham supplies vitamin B12 and niacin, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ham is often salty, so people with hypertension should limit consumption.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some brands use nitrites and other preservatives that may be undesirable with frequent intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The laminated pastry makes the product relatively high in calories; portion control is advised.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The pastry contains wheat, making it unsuitable for individuals with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the turnover in a microwave (≈ 1‑2 min) or in an oven at 180 °C (≈ 10‑12 min) until the crust is golden. Serve hot, optionally with a fresh salad, mustard, or your favorite dipping sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the original packaging in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months. Before heating, allow the product to thaw at room temperature for 10‑15 minutes.
